status_summary: The administration has acted on parts of this package through a memorandum, a statute and an exchange rule, but not through the prohibitions the chapter lists. The America First Investment Policy memorandum (2025-02-21) directs tools including CFIUS to restrict PRC-affiliated investment in technology, critical infrastructure and other strategic sectors, orders a review of expanded limits on U.S. outbound investment in sectors such as semiconductors, AI and quantum, directs fiduciary standards under ERISA aimed at making foreign adversary companies ineligible for pension plan contributions, and directs a review of audit standards and variable interest entity structures for China-based issuers; it does not itself direct delisting. Congress codified and expanded the Outbound Investment Security Program in Title LXXXV of Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 defense law (S. 1071), approved 2025-12-18, covering China and five other countries of concern, with Treasury regulations due within 450 days according to law-firm summaries; its exceptions include certain publicly traded securities and limited partner interests, and the existing program stays in force until then. On pensions, a Labor Department proposal published 2026-03-31 says only that fiduciaries cannot select an otherwise illegal investment, such as one in a foreign adversary on the OFAC sanctions list; it does not restrict Chinese stocks generally, and no rule barring pension funds from holding them was found. On listings, the SEC approved on an accelerated basis (notice published 2026-05-19) a Nasdaq rule adding initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China, including at least $25 million in U.S. offering proceeds or unrestricted public float; it applies to new listings and does not delist existing companies. No delisting program, closure of the A-shares market, or limit on Hong Kong clearinghouses or Chinese sovereign bonds was found. On the inbound side, Treasury asked on 2026-02-09 for input on streamlining CFIUS review through a Known Investor Program, the May 2026 state visit chartered a Board of Investment, and a law-firm alert of 2026-09-24 reports that board stalled, with Beijing seeking a pre-cleared list of industries and Washington preferring case-by-case review. On 2026-10-23 Treasury filed for public inspection a proposed rule implementing the statutory outbound program (91 FR 67396, publication scheduled 2026-10-26, comments due 2026-12-07); it is a proposal and at most a parallel match to the portfolio items, so the record stays in_progress 25 on the memorandum, the statute and the listing rule.

timeline.event: America First Investment Policy memorandum directs CFIUS and other tools against PRC-affiliated investment in strategic sectors, a review of outbound investment limits, ERISA fiduciary standards on foreign adversary holdings, and a review of audit standards and variable interest entities for China-based issuers.
SEC publishes Nasdaq's proposed rule adding initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China.

Public Law 119-60 (S. 1071), the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, is approved; its Title LXXXV, the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, covers sanctions, prohibition and notification of covered outbound transactions, and securities matters (table of contents). Law-firm summaries report it codifies and expands the Outbound Investment Security Program for China, including Hong Kong and Macau, with Treasury regulations due within 450 days.
Treasury's Office of Investment Security requests public input on streamlining CFIUS review, including through a Known Investor Program.

Labor Department's Employee Benefits Security Administration proposes a rule on fiduciary duties in selecting plan investment options that says fiduciaries cannot choose an otherwise illegal investment, such as one in a foreign adversary on the OFAC sanctions list.
White House fact sheet on a state visit to China says a U.S.-China Board of Investment is chartered as a government-to-government forum on investment-related issues.
SEC publishes its order granting accelerated approval to Nasdaq's initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China (as modified by Amendment No. 3).

Treasury's Office of Investment Security files for public inspection a proposed rule (filed 2026-10-23, scheduled for Federal Register publication 2026-10-26), Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations (91 FR 67396, docket TREAS-DO-2026-0595, RIN 1505-AC94; 31 CFR parts 850 and 851), implementing the statutory outbound program: notification and prohibition rules for U.S. persons' transactions with foreign persons in covered technologies, adding hypersonics, high-performance computing and biotechnology, and adding Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela to the PRC as countries of concern. Comments due 2026-12-07.

title: Limit Chinese investment, U.S. pension and portfolio flows to China, and Chinese listings
uncertainties: Public Law 119-60 was read on govinfo.gov only through its table of contents, which names Title LXXXV and its sections; the HTML carries no operative text of that title, so the 450-day regulation deadline and the exceptions for publicly traded securities and limited partner interests rest on law-firm summaries, and Sec. 8531 on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List was not read. Federal Register API queries by the researcher found no Treasury outbound investment rule or notice after 2025-01-29. The Nasdaq rule's contents were read from titles and short excerpts, so how strict the China criteria are is not stated. Federal Register searches on outbound investment, the Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act and ERISA foreign adversary rules found no Treasury, SEC or Labor action matching the pension, delisting, clearinghouse or sovereign bond items, but absence of a Federal Register document does not rule out other action (for example PCAOB or sanctions steps). Hong Kong clearinghouses and Chinese sovereign bonds were not searched beyond those queries. Overlaps c26-02, which holds the overall decoupling assessment. The Treasury outbound investment proposal filed for public inspection 2026-10-23 (publication scheduled 2026-10-26) is a parallel match at most: it would require notification of, or prohibit, U.S. persons' transactions with foreign persons in covered technologies in China and five other countries of concern, mostly through private and fund investment, and the part read (100,000 of about 133,000 characters) does not address pension holdings, listings, Hong Kong clearinghouses or sovereign bonds; it is only proposed, so the stage and progress are left as they are. The 2026-09-24 law-firm alert on the stalled Board of Investment is commentary, not a government action, so it was moved out of the timeline and is kept here and in sources as context.
